title: rover_gps_heading Software Requirements Specification
scope: rover_gps_heading provides rover_gps_heading_node, a C++ Clean Architecture node that derives the rover's absolute East-North-Up (ENU) heading from GNSS course while the rover drives straight. It estimates a fixed yaw offset between the local odom frame and ENU from gps/fix and odom, latches it once enough straight segments agree, and then republishes every odom yaw as an ENU heading on gps/heading_imu for rover_navsat_transform_node. It is localization logic, not a GPS driver: the receiver driver and fix-health diagnostics are in the sensor payload (rover_sensors, outside this boundary). It is started by rover_localization in GPS mode.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall subscribe to sensor_msgs/NavSatFix on the relative topic gps/fix with QoS reliable, volatile, keep-last depth 10.
requirements.rationale: GNSS fix is the project's reliable exception to best-effort sensor QoS: rover_gps_driver and the simulation bridge publish reliably, and navsat_transform subscribes reliably.
requirements.acceptance: `ros2 topic info -v gps/fix` shows the rover_gps_heading_node subscription as RELIABLE / VOLATILE, depth 10; the integration test SubscribesGpsFixReliably passes.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall subscribe to nav_msgs/Odometry on the relative topic odom (QoS depth 10) and use its orientation yaw, twist.linear.x and twist.angular.z.
requirements.rationale: The local EKF output (rover_ekf_node) provides the odom-frame yaw, forward speed and yaw rate used for straight-motion detection.
requirements.acceptance: Unit test OdometryToSample maps yaw, vx and yaw rate from an Odometry message; `ros2 topic info odom` lists rover_gps_heading_node as a subscriber.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall publish sensor_msgs/Imu on gps/heading_imu (QoS depth 10) with frame_id heading_frame_id, orientation containing only the ENU yaw (x = y = 0), orientation covariance [0] = [4] = 1.0e3 and [8] = yaw std squared, and angular-velocity and linear-acceleration covariance [0] = -1 (not provided).
requirements.rationale: navsat_transform_node needs an absolute ENU heading as an Imu message; -1 covariance marks the unused fields per the sensor_msgs convention (REP-103/REP-145 style).
requirements.acceptance: Unit test HeadingImuMessage passes; after alignment an echoed message has orientation.x = orientation.y = 0 and angular_velocity_covariance[0] = -1.
requirements.comments: Stamp is the node clock at publish time, not the odom message stamp (ros2_heading_publisher.cpp:46) [TBC whether this matters for navsat_transform].

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall publish gps/heading_imu only after the alignment has reached the Aligned state and only when publish_heading is true, and then once for every received odom message with yaw = wrap(odom yaw + latched offset).
requirements.rationale: An unaligned heading would place GPS fixes wrongly in the map frame.
requirements.acceptance: Integration test: no gps/heading_imu before alignment; after a simulated straight drive meeting the alignment conditions, messages are published with the expected ENU yaw; with publish_heading=false nothing is published.
requirements.comments: Output rate therefore equals the odom rate (rover_ekf_node, 50 Hz per rover_localization config).

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall form one course measurement from each straight segment of at least alignment.min_segment_length_m (3.0 m) GNSS displacement, as offset = atan2(dNorth, dEast) - circular mean of odom yaw over the segment, adding pi when reversing (vx < 0).
requirements.rationale: While not turning, the GNSS course equals the ENU heading and the antenna lever arm does not bias it.
requirements.acceptance: Unit tests AlignsWhileDrivingStraight, ReversingAddsHalfTurn and OffsetAcrossWrapAround pass.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall treat motion as straight only when |vx| >= alignment.min_speed_m_s (0.3 m/s), |yaw rate| <= alignment.max_yaw_rate_rad_s (0.1 rad/s) and the yaw change since segment start is <= alignment.max_yaw_change_rad (0.1 rad), and shall abort the current segment otherwise or when the drive direction changes.
requirements.rationale: Course equals heading only for straight motion.
requirements.acceptance: Unit tests TurningIsRejected and StandingStillIsRejected pass (no segment accepted).

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall ignore a GNSS fix for alignment (and abort the current segment) when it has no fix status, its horizontal 1-sigma error exceeds alignment.max_horizontal_std_m (5.0 m), the latest odometry is older than alignment.max_odometry_age_s (0.5 s), or the gap to the previous fix exceeds alignment.max_fix_gap_s (2.5 s).
requirements.rationale: Poor or stale fixes would corrupt the course measurement.
requirements.acceptance: Unit test NoFixIsIgnored passes; unit test UnknownCovarianceAndNoFix maps STATUS_NO_FIX and unknown covariance correctly.
requirements.comments: A fix with unknown covariance (horizontal std NaN) is accepted (heading_alignment_estimator.cpp:86-87).

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall latch the circular mean of the most recent alignment.required_segments (3) offsets as the odom-to-ENU yaw offset when their circular standard deviation is <= alignment.max_offset_std_rad (0.1 rad), and keep it until reset.
requirements.rationale: Agreement of several independent segments guards against a single bad measurement.
requirements.acceptance: Unit tests AlignsWhileDrivingStraight and NotAlignedBeforeEnoughSegments pass; after alignment further fixes do not change the offset.
requirements.comments: No re-validation after latching: a drifting odom yaw (IMU gyro drift) is not corrected until a manual reset [TBC].

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall report the published heading standard deviation as max(min_heading_std_rad, latched offset std), with min_heading_std_rad = 0.05 rad by default.
requirements.rationale: Prevents over-confident heading covariance in navsat_transform and the global EKF.
requirements.acceptance: Unit test PublishesEnuHeadingOnceAligned passes; published orientation_covariance[8] >= 0.05^2.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall provide the std_srvs/Trigger service gps/reset_heading_alignment that discards the alignment, returns success true with the message 'Heading alignment reset; drive straight to realign.', and immediately republishes the (unaligned) alignment status.
requirements.rationale: Lets the operator realign after a heading error without restarting the node.
requirements.acceptance: Integration test: calling the service after alignment returns success and gps/heading_imu stops until a new alignment; unit test ResetClearsAlignment passes.
requirements.derived_rationale: Technical operability interface of the alignment.
requirements.comments: rover_navsat_transform_node computes its transform only once, so it must be restarted after a reset (rover_gps_heading/README.md:39-40).

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall publish a 'Heading alignment' diagnostic (hardware ID 'RoverGpsHeading') with keys State, Accepted segments, Heading output and, once available, Yaw offset (deg) and Offset std (deg), updated by a 1 s timer and immediately at startup and on alignment.
requirements.rationale: Shows the operator whether GPS fusion has an absolute heading (SYS-SR-022 sensor diagnostics).
requirements.acceptance: Within 2 s of start, <ns>/diagnostics contains 'rover_gps_heading_node: Heading alignment' with the State key; updates arrive at >= 1 Hz.
requirements.comments: The tick timer is a wall timer (1 s). Grouped under /Rover/GPS by rover_diag_manager.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall grade the 'Heading alignment' diagnostic OK when aligned, OK when unaligned with publish_heading false, and WARN ('Drive straight to align the GNSS heading.') when unaligned with publish_heading true.
requirements.rationale: An unaligned heading is only a fault when GPS fusion depends on it.
requirements.acceptance: Integration tests WarnsWhileUnaligned and HeadingOutputDisabled pass.
requirements.comments: Never reports ERROR, and does not go STALE when gps/fix or odom stop arriving after alignment.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall declare publish_heading (default true), min_heading_std_rad (default 0.05, positive, max 3.2), heading_frame_id (default base_link) and the alignment.* parameters with the defaults min_segment_length_m 3.0, min_speed_m_s 0.3, max_yaw_rate_rad_s 0.1, max_yaw_change_rad 0.1, max_horizontal_std_m 5.0, max_fix_gap_s 2.5, max_odometry_age_s 0.5, required_segments 3 (range 1-100) and max_offset_std_rad 0.1.
requirements.rationale: Declared, bounded parameters prevent silent misconfiguration.
requirements.acceptance: `ros2 param describe` shows each parameter with its range; the defaults match the HeadingAlignmentConfig struct.
requirements.comments: README.md:59 says all parameters are read-only; no on-set-parameters callback exists, so runtime changes have no effect.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall validate the alignment configuration at construction, rejecting non-positive limits or required_segments = 0, and shall then exit with code 1 and a FATAL log.
requirements.rationale: Fail fast on inconsistent configuration instead of at the first fix.
requirements.acceptance: Integration test RejectsInvalidAlignmentConfig and unit test RejectsInvalidConfig pass; starting with alignment.min_speed_m_s:=0.0 exits with code 1.
requirements.comments: Plain rclcpp::Node (not lifecycle); it owns no hardware resource.

requirements.text: The rover_gps_heading shall keep its domain and application code (geo math, HeadingAlignmentEstimator, AlignHeadingUseCase) in the rover_gps_heading_core static library without ROS dependencies.
requirements.rationale: Clean Architecture: the alignment logic is unit-testable without a ROS graph.
requirements.acceptance: rover_gps_heading_core sources include no rclcpp or *_msgs header; its unit tests link only the core library.
